identity.name: AzureHound Cloud-Identity Enumeration Stitch: Token Theft -> Non-Interactive Entra Sign-In -> Bulk Microsoft Graph Discovery (SIM-MP-014)
identity.summary: A stolen cloud refresh token, an anomalous non-interactive Entra ID sign-in from an unusual geo, and an AzureHound-user-agent Microsoft Graph enumeration burst collapse to one XSIAM incident on a shared session identity — proving cross-plane causality across endpoint, cloud identity, and cloud-audit telemetry instead of three low-fidelity alerts.
identity.description: Curious Serpens (Peach Sandstorm), Void Blizzard, and Storm-0501 have all been observed misusing AzureHound — the Go data collector for BloodHound — for post-compromise discovery of a target's Microsoft Entra ID tenant. The chain begins on the endpoint: an infostealer such as Raccoon Stealer or Redline extracts cookies, credentials, and session tokens from a user's browser credential stores (T1528). That stolen session token is replayed against login.microsoftonline.com to obtain a non-interactive sign-in (T1078.004) that Entra records in its non-interactive sign-in logs — frequently from an unusual geography (impossible travel from the identity's baseline) because the operator is elsewhere. AzureHound then drives a high-volume Microsoft Graph enumeration burst (`azurehound list users|groups|service-principals|role-assignments|key-vaults|storage-accounts`) that shows up in Microsoft Graph activity logs carrying the distinctive `azurehound/<version>` User-Agent (e.g. `azurehound/v2.6.0`), typically preceded by a `GET /v1.0/organization` reachability probe and exceeding 500 Graph calls/hour. The output lands on disk as `users.json`, `groups.json`, etc. for ingest into BloodHound. A critical blind spot: the Azure Resource Manager list calls AzureHound makes against management.azure.com (storage-accounts, key-vaults, virtual-machines) are NOT recorded in Azure Activity Logs, so the Graph-side volume and the non-interactive sign-in are the load-bearing signals. This card is CORRELATION-terminal: two ABIOCs (anomalous non-interactive sign-in, AzureHound Graph enumeration burst) plus an endpoint token-theft BIOC are stitched by CR-MP-0014 on the shared session identity (endpoint actor -> Entra user_principal_name -> cloud_audit identity_name, joined via signin_activity_id / caller_ip) into a single escalation incident whose causality chain spans the endpoint, cloud-identity, and cloud-audit planes.

campaigns: Iranian-nexus cloud-identity discovery against Entra ID tenants (2024-2026)
Ransomware operator hybrid multi-tenant Entra enumeration

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-MP-014 — AzureHound cloud-identity enumeration cross-plane stitch (token theft -> non-interactive Entra sign-in -> bulk Graph discovery).

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agent installed on the jumpbox so endpoint file-access and process telemetry reaches xdr_data.
Entra ID sign-in logs and Microsoft Graph activity logs ingested into XSIAM (Graph activity logging is GA April 2024 but disabled by default).
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'confirm msft_azure_ad_signin and cloud_audit_logs datasets are ingesting in the tenant'

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE: no real token theft, no real Entra/Graph egress. All signals are
# modelled with local marker files under the identity harness so XSIAM sees the
# process/file causality shape without touching a real cloud tenant.
set -euo pipefail
WORK="${WORK_DIR:-/tmp/cortexsim_mp014}"
mkdir -p "$WORK"
# (1) endpoint token theft — model an infostealer sweeping browser credential
# stores (saved logins + cookie/session-token DBs) with a non-browser process
printf 'SAFE-MODE-COOKIE-MARKER-NOT-A-REAL-SESSION-TOKEN\n' > "$WORK/cookies.sqlite"
printf 'SAFE-MODE-LOGIN-MARKER-NOT-A-REAL-CREDENTIAL\n' > "$WORK/Login Data"
grep -a 'SAFE-MODE' "$WORK/cookies.sqlite" "$WORK/Login Data" | head -2
# (2) model AzureHound Graph enumeration output artifacts on disk
for obj in users groups service-principals role-assignments key-vaults storage-accounts; do
  printf '{"marker":"SAFE-MODE azurehound list %s"}\n' "$obj" > "$WORK/${obj}.json"
done
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-MP-014 chain modelled: token-cache read + azurehound-style JSON artifacts staged.'

input_variables.name: WORK_DIR
input_variables.description: Scratch directory the SAFE-MODE browser-credential-store markers and modelled AzureHound JSON artifacts are written to.

expected_artifacts.description: A non-browser process reading multiple browser credential/cookie stores under the run identity (models infostealer browser session-token theft).
expected_artifacts.expected_value: action_file_path contains "cookies.sqlite" or action_file_path contains "Login Data"

expected_artifacts.description: A non-interactive Entra ID sign-in from an unusual geography (impossible travel from the identity's baseline) on the same user principal.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: is_interactive = false and location_country deviates from the identity's learned sign-in baseline

expected_artifacts.description: A burst of Microsoft Graph GET calls carrying the azurehound User-Agent exceeding 500 requests/hour.

iocs.context: AzureHound emits a distinctive HTTP User-Agent 'azurehound/<version>' (e.g. azurehound/v2.6.0) on its Microsoft Graph and Azure Resource Manager calls. Match case-insensitively; version suffix varies.

biocs.name: MP-014 Browser Session-Token and Cookie Theft by Non-Browser Process
biocs.description: A non-browser process reads multiple browser credential stores (saved-login and cookie/session-token databases). Infostealers such as Raccoon Stealer or Redline sweep these stores to lift session tokens later replayed against Entra ID; the browser reading its own store is normal, a non-browser process sweeping several stores in one burst is the endpoint anchor of the AzureHound chain.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type = ENUM.FILE_OPEN
| filter action_file_path contains "Login Data" or action_file_path contains "cookies.sqlite" or action_file_path contains "logins.json" or action_file_path contains "key4.db"
| filter actor_process_image_name not in ("chrome", "chromium", "google-chrome", "msedge", "firefox", "firefox-bin", "cortex-agent")
| comp count_distinct(action_file_path) as stores_read by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id
| filter stores_read >= 2
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, actor_process_image_name, actor_process_instance_id, stores_read

biocs.name: MP-014 AzureHound Microsoft Graph Reachability Probe
biocs.description: AzureHound issues a GET /v1.0/organization reachability probe against graph.microsoft.com before the bulk enumeration begins. Paired with the azurehound User-Agent this is an early, low-volume tell of the enumeration about to start.
biocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter lowercase(user_agent) contains "azurehound"
| filter request_uri contains "/v1.0/organization" or request_uri contains "graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/organization"
| comp count() as probe_calls by identity_name, caller_ip, user_agent
| filter probe_calls >= 1
| fields identity_name, caller_ip, user_agent, probe_calls

xql_queries.name: MP-014 AzureHound User-Agent Present in Cloud Audit Logs
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter lowercase(user_agent) contains "azurehound"
| comp count() as azurehound_calls by identity_name, caller_ip, user_agent
| filter azurehound_calls >= 1
| fields identity_name, caller_ip, user_agent, azurehound_calls

xql_queries.name: MP-014 High-Volume Graph Enumeration Above 500 Calls Per Hour
xql_queries.query:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| filter http_method = "GET"
| filter request_uri contains "graph.microsoft.com"
| bin _time span = 60m
| comp count() as api_call_count by identity_name, user_agent, caller_ip, _time
| filter api_call_count > 500
| sort desc api_call_count
| fields identity_name, user_agent, caller_ip, api_call_count

xql_queries.name: MP-014 Cross-Plane Stitch Single Incident Spanning Endpoint and Cloud Identity
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 3600)
| comp count_distinct(_product) as plane_count, count_distinct(incident_id) as incident_count by causality_actor_primary_username
| filter plane_count >= 2 and incident_count = 1
| fields causality_actor_primary_username, plane_count, incident_count

abiocs.name: MP-014 Non-Interactive Entra Sign-In from Unusual Geo Post Token Theft
abiocs.description: A non-interactive Entra ID sign-in (stolen session/refresh-token replay) lands on a user principal from a geography that deviates from that identity's learned sign-in baseline (impossible travel). The ABIOC anchors the deviation to the cloud-identity profile (non-interactive token replay diverging from the user's usual interactive, in-region sign-ins) rather than to any single bad value.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = msft_azure_ad_signin
| filter is_interactive = false
| comp count() as noninteractive_signins, values(signin_activity_id) as signin_activity_ids, count_distinct(location_country) as geo_count by user_principal_name, ip_address, app_display_name
| filter geo_count >= 2
| fields user_principal_name, ip_address, app_display_name, noninteractive_signins, geo_count, signin_activity_ids
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-identity Entra sign-in baseline (interactive, in-region, known apps) -> stolen-token replay produces a non-interactive, out-of-region sign-in (impossible travel) that diverges from the baseline, anchored to the user_principal_name and signin_activity_id.

abiocs.name: MP-014 AzureHound Bulk Microsoft Graph Enumeration Burst
abiocs.description: A single identity drives a high-volume burst of Microsoft Graph GET enumeration (users, groups, roleManagement) carrying the azurehound User-Agent, far exceeding that identity's learned Graph read cadence. Every call is a legitimate Graph read; the ABIOC fires on the volumetric-and-cadence deviation from the identity's learned baseline, anchored to the caller identity and session.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = cloud_audit_logs
| filter http_method = "GET"
| filter request_uri contains "graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users" or request_uri contains "graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/groups" or request_uri contains "graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement" or lowercase(user_agent) contains "azurehound"
| bin _time span = 60m
| comp count() as graph_calls by identity_name, user_agent, caller_ip, _time
| filter graph_calls > 500
| sort desc graph_calls
| fields identity_name, user_agent, caller_ip, graph_calls
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-identity Microsoft Graph read cadence -> AzureHound enumeration burst (>500 GET/hour across users/groups/roles) that exceeds the identity's learned volume, anchored to identity_name + caller_ip and correlated to the sign-in via signin_activity_id.

correlation_rules.name: AzureHound Cloud-Identity Enumeration Chain — Token Theft to Graph Discovery Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: BIOC(MP-014 Browser Session-Token and Cookie Theft by Non-Browser Process) AND ABIOC(MP-014 Non-Interactive Entra Sign-In from Unusual Geo Post Token Theft) AND ABIOC(MP-014 AzureHound Bulk Microsoft Graph Enumeration Burst) within a 30-minute window, joined on the shared session identity (endpoint actor_effective_username maps to Entra user_principal_name maps to cloud_audit_logs identity_name, correlated by signin_activity_id and caller_ip). Fuses the endpoint token-theft signal, the anomalous non-interactive cloud sign-in, and the AzureHound Graph enumeration burst into a single escalation incident spanning the endpoint, cloud-identity, and cloud-audit planes instead of three low-fidelity alerts.

threat_scenarios.name: AzureHound Cloud-Identity Enumeration — Cross-Plane Causality Stitch
threat_scenarios.description: Prove that Cortex stitches an endpoint token-theft signal, an anomalous non-interactive Entra ID sign-in, and an AzureHound-user-agent Microsoft Graph enumeration burst into one escalation incident on a shared session identity — the cross-plane causality a single-plane tool sees only as three disconnected low-fidelity alerts.

threat_steps.objective: The endpoint token-theft BIOC and the anomalous non-interactive Entra sign-in ABIOC both fire on the same identity.
preconditions: Jumpbox with the Cortex agent installed.
Entra ID non-interactive sign-in logs ingesting into msft_azure_ad_signin.
steps: Run the SAFE-MODE token-cache read step under the identity harness.
Emit the modelled non-interactive at-risk Entra sign-in on the same user principal.
Observe the BIOC and the sign-in ABIOC fire.
success_criteria: BIOC `MP-014 Browser Session-Token and Cookie Theft by Non-Browser Process` fires.
ABIOC `MP-014 Non-Interactive Entra Sign-In from Unusual Geo Post Token Theft` fires.

threat_steps.objective: The AzureHound Graph enumeration burst is detected by volume and by the azurehound User-Agent.
preconditions: Microsoft Graph activity logging enabled and ingesting into cloud_audit_logs.
steps: Model the AzureHound bulk Graph enumeration burst (>500 GET/hour, azurehound User-Agent).
Run the validation XQL for the azurehound User-Agent.
success_criteria: ABIOC `MP-014 AzureHound Bulk Microsoft Graph Enumeration Burst` fires.
XQL `MP-014 AzureHound User-Agent Present in Cloud Audit Logs` returns the enumerating identity.

threat_steps.objective: The three signals stitch into a single incident whose causality chain spans at least two planes.
preconditions: All three plane telemetry sources ingesting; correlation window >= 30 minutes.
steps: Let the XSIAM correlation engine converge on the shared session identity.
Assert one incident_id spans the endpoint and cloud-identity planes.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-MP-0014` raises exactly one stitched incident.
The incident's causality chain spans >= 2 planes (endpoint + cloud identity/audit).

preventive_controls: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA and Entra ID Token Protection (GA August 2025) so a stolen refresh token cannot be replayed from a new device/session.
Apply Conditional Access Policies and Privileged Identity Management to gate non-interactive sign-ins and privileged Graph scopes.
Deploy EDR/XDR across all endpoints — including cloud workloads — to catch token-cache theft at the source, and disable user-initiated app registrations.
detection_engineering: Enable Microsoft Graph activity logging (disabled by default) so bulk Graph enumeration is visible in cloud_audit_logs.
Alert on the azurehound User-Agent and on any identity exceeding ~500 Graph GET calls/hour against users/groups/roleManagement.

Correlate non-interactive, out-of-region Entra sign-ins with endpoint browser-credential-store access and cloud-audit enumeration on the shared session identity (signin_activity_id / caller_ip) rather than alerting on each in isolation.
Note the ARM blind spot: management.azure.com list/GET calls AzureHound makes are NOT in Azure Activity Logs, so weight the Graph-side volume and the sign-in signal accordingly.
